result:
Solution 3 is correct. Each pair of distinct circles meets in at most 2 points, and there are C(4,2) = 6 pairs, so there are at most 12 intersection points. Twelve is achievable: take four circles with generic centers and radii, so that every pair meets in two points and no three circles share a point.

Solution 1 gives 10, which is too low because its clover arrangement doesn't use the full capacity of the opposite pairs. Solution 2 gives 14, which exceeds the bound of 12. Its claim that a fourth circle can pass through A and B and meet each other circle in two new points is impossible, since A and B are already shared by three circles, so the new intersections are not all distinct.

CHOICE: 3
